title: Our process — Supreme Art
description: Follow every carton through Pre press, Press and Offpress at Supreme Art, from artwork and plate preparation to finishing and delivery.
intro: Scroll through every stage — from the initial design to the packed cartons delivered to your facility, each production step is carefully controlled under one roof in Peshawar.

steps.title: Designing
steps.text: Artwork and carton layouts are created and prepared by our in-house design team.

steps.title: Plate making
steps.text: Using our computer-to-plate (CTP) system, printing plates are produced for the offset press.

steps.title: Cutting
steps.text: Stock paperboard is cut to the precise sheet size required by the printing machine.

steps.title: Printing
steps.text: The approved carton design is printed onto the prepared sheets using offset printing presses.

steps.title: Proofing & QC
steps.text: Our quality-control team checks colour shades, registration and text content against the approved proof.

steps.title: Coating
steps.text: The printed sheets receive the specified protective or decorative coating for the required finish.

steps.title: Die-cutting
steps.text: The coated sheets are cut and creased into individual unit-carton blanks.

steps.title: Breaking
steps.text: Waste board is removed from around the die-cut cartons, separating the individual blanks cleanly.

steps.title: Sorting
steps.text: An automated inspection machine uses 3D cameras to check every unit carton for colour, print and overall quality.

steps.title: Pasting & folder gluing
steps.text: The inspected unit cartons are folded, glued and joined before being packed into bundles or boxes.

steps.title: Delivery
steps.text: The finished cartons are securely packed and delivered to the client, ready for the filling line.

cta.heading: Have a carton to make?
cta.text: Send us your artwork or dieline — we'll come back with a quote and a timeline.

prepress.detail: Our designers bring the artwork and carton layout together on screen, carefully arranging the text, colour and panels before the design moves into production.
prepress.alt: Designer preparing a carton layout on a computer monitor.

prepress.detail: The artwork moves into computer-to-plate preparation. A blue-coated aluminium plate carries the image that the offset press will use to reproduce the design.
prepress.alt: Blue printing plate loaded into the computer-to-plate equipment.

prepress.detail: The prepared plate travels through the processor. Controlled cleaning removes the unwanted coating and leaves the image areas needed for printing.
prepress.alt: Blue plate passing through the rollers of the plate processor.

prepress.detail: The plate emerges with the image areas visible on its surface. It is now ready for checking and the next step at the printing press.
prepress.alt: Processed aluminium plate emerging with blue image areas visible.

prepress.detail: Alongside plate preparation, the paperboard is readied for production. Wrapped stacks keep the sheets together until they are needed for the job.
prepress.alt: Wrapped paperboard stacks stored on wooden pallets.

prepress.detail: A pallet lifter carries the paperboard from storage to the cutting area. The stack stays supported as it moves to the next part of the process.
prepress.alt: Operator moving a pallet of paperboard using a yellow pallet lifter.

prepress.detail: The operator aligns the paperboard at the guillotine, where the stack is cut to the sheet size required for the job. With plates and sheets prepared, everything is ready for Press.
prepress.alt: Operator aligning a paperboard stack at the guillotine cutting machine.

press.text: The prepared plates transfer the approved artwork onto the cut sheets using offset printing. Colour, registration and printed detail are checked against the approved proof as the job progresses.

press.alt: Press operator loading ink tins on top of the printing units.
press.text: Before the run begins, the printer charges each unit with ink, preparing the process and spot colours the job needs.

press.alt: Multi-colour offset press line with a stack of paperboard at the feeder.
press.text: Each colour has its own printing unit. The sheet travels through them in sequence, taking on one ink after another.

press.alt: Operator starting the press beside printed sheets on the delivery table.
press.text: With the cut sheets loaded at the feeder, the operator starts the run, and the first printed sheets arrive at the delivery for review.

press.alt: Heidelberg Speedmaster CD 102 multi-colour printing press.
press.text: Our Heidelberg Speedmaster CD 102 prints multi-colour work at production speed with consistent registration from sheet to sheet.

press.alt: Operator measuring a printed sheet with a handheld spectrophotometer.
press.text: Colour is measured, not guessed. A handheld spectrophotometer reads the printed sheet and compares it with the approved colour targets.

press.alt: Operator comparing a printed sheet with the approved proof at the press console.
press.text: At the console, the printed sheet is checked against the approved proof, and the ink zones are adjusted until every carton on the sheet matches.

press.alt: Operator at the controls of Offset Machine 3, a Heidelberg SM-74.
press.text: Offset Machine 3, a Heidelberg SM-74, handles smaller sheet formats alongside our larger Speedmaster line, so each job runs on the right press.

offpress.text: The printed sheets receive the specified protective or decorative coating for the required finish.
The coated sheets are cut and creased into individual unit-carton blanks.
Waste board is removed from around the die-cut cartons, separating the individual blanks cleanly.
An automated inspection machine uses 3D cameras to check every unit carton for colour, print and overall quality.

offpress.alt: Pasting & folder gluing equipment and production.
offpress.text: The inspected unit cartons are folded, glued and joined before being packed into bundles or boxes.
The finished cartons are securely packed and delivered to the client, ready for the filling line.

prepress_groups.detail: Our designers prepare the carton layout, arranging its panels, text and colours on screen. Printed artwork is then reviewed alongside the samples, so the layout and details can be checked before plate preparation.
